title: What Is a Patent Worth? Evidence from the U.S. Patent “Lottery”
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; identification; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates the value of patent rights from invention quality, then aligns the IV assumptions, threats, external validity, and financing channel with that estimand.
transfer_limit: Examiner-leniency arguments are design-specific and cannot be transplanted to an unrelated IV.

title: The Loan Covenant Channel: How Bank Health Transmits to the Real Economy
selected_sections: introduction; design triangulation; results; aggregate interpretation
teaching_function: Turns the apparent durability of long-term loans into a puzzle and uses complementary designs to move from lending adjustments to real and aggregate consequences.
transfer_limit: The aggregate decomposition and unusually long front matter depend on special supervisory data and are not a default template.

title: Lender Automation and Racial Disparities in Credit Access
selected_sections: introduction; mechanisms; alternative explanations; results
teaching_function: Prestates competing channels and assigns distinct data and tests to each, so the evidence narrows explanations rather than relabeling heterogeneity after the fact.
transfer_limit: The evidence blocks do not all have identical causal strength, and the long introduction should not be copied as a length target.

title: Personal Communication in an Automated World: Evidence from Loan Repayments
selected_sections: abstract; selection-versus-process distinction; external validity
teaching_function: Distinguishes nonrandom contact from operational variation in completed communication and keeps mechanism, persistence, and scope separate.
transfer_limit: The conclusion is unusually thin and some mechanism evidence is suggestive, so use it only for the named functions.

title: What Is the Cost of Privatization for Workers?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; benefit-cost evidence chain; conclusion
teaching_function: Presents worker costs and firm benefits in the same argument and sequences baseline effects, alternative definitions, heterogeneity, and policy mitigation.
transfer_limit: The benefit-cost framing is not a complete social-welfare calculation and remains conditional on the design.

title: Taming the Factor Zoo: A Test of New Factors
selected_sections: introduction; method exposition; validation; robustness
teaching_function: Builds a clean problem-to-method chain around why existing factor tests fail and organizes validation around tuning, test assets, and model selection.
transfer_limit: Its high-dimensional terminology and particular estimator are not requirements for ordinary asset-pricing papers.

title: Duration-Driven Returns
selected_sections: introduction; evidence order; identification; mechanisms
teaching_function: Orders cash-flow facts, a duration factor, conventional asset tests, dividend-strip identification, and bond evidence so each layer narrows the explanation set.
transfer_limit: The unusually rich dividend-futures evidence is not a required number of tests for other papers.

title: Measuring “Dark Matter” in Asset Pricing Models
selected_sections: concept introduction; formal definition; applications; conclusion
teaching_function: Moves from a motivating example to a formal diagnostic, explains why the object matters, and then translates it into model-choice and data-collection implications.
transfer_limit: The object is abstract; use this for concept exposition, not as a generic abstract or introduction template.

title: Relationship Trading in Over-the-Counter Markets
selected_sections: facts-to-model bridge; structural identification; fit; policy counterfactual
teaching_function: Gives descriptive facts, the model, structural estimation, parameter identification, fit, sensitivity, and policy analysis distinct evidentiary jobs.
transfer_limit: The policy and welfare interpretation is conditional on the OTC model and is not a reduced-form template.

title: Bank Market Power and Monetary Policy Transmission: Evidence from a Structural Estimation
selected_sections: introduction; friction-channel map; parameter mapping; counterfactuals
teaching_function: Maps several banking frictions into distinct transmission channels, estimates them, removes them one at a time, and checks the resulting model externally.
transfer_limit: Model-implied decompositions must remain conditional on identification, fit, and maintained structure.

title: A Model of Systemic Bank Runs
selected_sections: abstract; mechanism loop; model progression; policy mapping
teaching_function: Compresses within-bank coordination and cross-bank price externalities into a feedback loop, then develops liquid-asset, uncertainty, and policy extensions.
transfer_limit: The paper and literature positioning are long; learn the mechanism map, not its length or section granularity.

title: Decentralized Exchange: The Uniswap Automated Market Maker
selected_sections: institutional exposition; theory-empirics bridge; market comparison
teaching_function: Explains an unfamiliar market institution before stating its central tradeoff and mapping the framework to comprehensive transaction data.
transfer_limit: The protocol and smart-contract details are institution-specific and should not become generic market-design requirements.

title: Finance without exotic risk
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; results synthesis; conclusion
teaching_function: Starts from the joint-hypothesis problem, explains a measurement innovation and its limits, and sequences three result families before returning to the economic interpretation.
transfer_limit: The debate is field-wide and the claims are strong; narrower papers should not imitate its exclusivity or length.

title: A quantitative analysis of bank lending relationships
selected_sections: abstract; model-data mapping; validation; shocks; conclusion
teaching_function: Separates empirical motivation, model construction, directly estimated parameters, untargeted validation, mechanism comparisons, and aggregate shocks.
transfer_limit: Its long introduction and multi-layer model fit quantitative work, not a short reduced-form paper.

title: Price regulation in two-sided markets: Empirical evidence from debit cards
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; multi-side results; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Defines the two-sided policy problem and reports transmission in the order banks, merchants, and consumers, while keeping welfare claims within observed outcomes.
transfer_limit: Do not infer total welfare from one side's price or quantity when other margins are unobserved.

title: The death of a regulator: Strict supervision, bank lending, and business activity
selected_sections: introduction; competing channels; results order; external validity; conclusion
teaching_function: Frames credit contraction and improved management as competing consequences of stricter supervision, then organizes evidence to distinguish them.
transfer_limit: The regulator transition is rare and the long introduction is an argument map, not a fixed paragraph template.

title: How does competition affect retail banking? Quasi-experimental evidence from bank mergers
selected_sections: introduction; assumptions; placebo; heterogeneous outcomes; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes the threshold, first stage, identifying assumptions, placebo evidence, and local scope visible while preserving different results across products.
transfer_limit: The merger-threshold estimate is local and should not become a universal statement that competition is beneficial.

title: Limited attention to detail in financial markets: Evidence from reduced-form and structural estimation
selected_sections: abstract; reused-design confounds; reduced-form-structural triangulation
teaching_function: Shows how to reuse an existing natural experiment responsibly by listing new confounds and using additional evidence plus a structural model to quantify them.
transfer_limit: A structural model solves specific interpretation problems here; it is not a compulsory add-on to every natural experiment.

title: Sorting out the effect of credit supply
selected_sections: abstract; facts-to-model bridge; identification; decomposition; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses nonrandom bank-firm matching to motivate an assignment model and makes the model responsible for separating supply from demand.
transfer_limit: The recovered supply share depends on functional-form and identification assumptions and is not model-free.

title: Competition and selection in credit markets
selected_sections: abstract; counterintuitive hook; predictions; alternatives; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns a counterintuitive pricing prediction into mechanism-specific heterogeneity and administrative-data tests, then treats alternative channels together.
transfer_limit: The selection-cost mechanism and risky-borrower conditions limit any general policy claim about competition.

title: Corporate culture: Evidence from the field
selected_sections: abstract; construct definition; validation; placebo; limitations
teaching_function: Demonstrates how a noncausal survey paper can earn credibility by distinguishing constructs, validating measures externally, and stating selection and response-bias limits.
transfer_limit: Executive beliefs and correlations cannot be rewritten as evidence that culture causes firm value.

title: On the direct and indirect real effects of credit supply shocks
selected_sections: identification threats; out-of-sample validation; channels; equilibrium effects
teaching_function: Estimates the shock, discusses threats, validates it on loan applications outside the estimation sample, and only then reports direct, network, and price channels.
transfer_limit: The network decomposition requires unusually comprehensive administrative and input-output data and does not make each channel exclusive.

title: Sticking to your plan
selected_sections: abstract; model-to-measure bridge; robustness; alternative interpretations
teaching_function: Uses a parsimonious model to show how high-frequency behavior maps to impatience and sophistication, then derives classifications and predictions for the data.
transfer_limit: A behavioral proxy alone does not identify present bias; the construct remains model- and data-dependent.

title: Asset Pricing: A Tale of Night and Day
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; result narration; discussion; conclusion
teaching_function: Decomposes an apparent full-day pricing failure into opposing daytime and overnight relations and keeps the final mechanism interpretation cautious.
transfer_limit: Use it for puzzle decomposition and readable results, not as a complete causal-mechanism template.

title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; out-of-sample evidence; economic value
teaching_function: Translates a method comparison into out-of-sample prediction, investor value, variable importance, and implications for measuring expected returns.
transfer_limit: A model tournament or Sharpe improvement is not a required contribution for every asset-pricing paper.

title: The Rate of Return on Real Estate: Long-Run Micro-Level Evidence
selected_sections: abstract; measurement audit; benchmarks; result decomposition
teaching_function: Writes the paper as an audit of a historically mismeasured object and uses unique micro records plus transparent benchmarks to map the evidence.
transfer_limit: The archival setting is exceptional and the paper is not a causal-identification template.

title: Do Neighborhoods Affect the Credit Market Decisions of Low-Income Borrowers? Evidence from the Moving to Opportunity Experiment
selected_sections: abstract; experimental design; long-run outcomes; mechanisms
teaching_function: Defines the causal object and treatment arms clearly, links random assignment to long-run credit records, and separates direct effects from income-related channels.
transfer_limit: Mechanism language must remain tied to what the randomized treatment changes; subgroup differences alone are insufficient.

title: Does Career Risk Deter Potential Entrepreneurs?
selected_sections: abstract; cutoff explanation; validity; rule-in and rule-out tests
teaching_function: Makes a cutoff design intuitive and evaluates two competing mechanism accounts with separate rule-out and rule-in evidence.
transfer_limit: The local discontinuity effect cannot be generalized to all potential entrepreneurs.

title: Financial Crises and the Transmission of Monetary Policy to Consumer Credit Markets
selected_sections: introduction; theory ambiguity; IV design; placebo; external validity
teaching_function: Uses competing model predictions to establish why the sign is ambiguous, then lets IV evidence, placebos, and channel tests resolve the question.
transfer_limit: The institution and lender type limit representativeness beyond the studied consumer-credit market.

title: Digital Payments and Consumption: Evidence from the 2016 Demonetization in India
selected_sections: abstract; design; threat-driven validation; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Compresses the shock, first stage, main magnitude, persistence, and mechanism into the abstract and assigns tests to explicit parallel-trend and exclusion threats.
transfer_limit: The demonetization shock is unusual; the number of robustness tests is not itself a quality target.

title: How Does Removing the Tax Benefits of Debt Affect Firms? Evidence from the 2017 U.S. Tax Reform
selected_sections: abstract; validity; magnitude; falsification; conclusion
teaching_function: Keeps threshold validity, predetermined characteristics, alternative accounts, magnitudes, and falsifications in a coherent evidence order.
transfer_limit: The estimand remains local to the threshold and the unusually long conclusion is not a length model.

title: Bank Cleanups, Capitalization, and Lending: Evidence from India
selected_sections: abstract; policy tradeoff; channels; real effects
teaching_function: Shows how to state the intended informational benefit of a bank cleanup, the missing recapitalization condition, subsequent bank behavior, and real effects as one policy chain.
transfer_limit: The institutional exercise and data are special, and the long evidence chain should not be treated as a generic causal-paper template.
metadata_note: Used instead of an online-2025/print-2026 candidate to keep the selected set within print years 2020–2025.

title: Bond Price Fragility and the Structure of the Mutual Fund Industry
selected_sections: abstract; framework; main results; mechanisms; alternatives; stabilizing evidence
teaching_function: Uses calibrated wording and moves from a framework to fragility evidence, mechanisms, alternatives, a policy shock, and offsetting stabilizing trades.
transfer_limit: Mechanism evidence narrows interpretations but does not establish one exclusive causal channel.
metadata_note: Canonical year is 2024; the local source folder is 2023.

title: Production Networks and Stock Returns: The Role of Vertical Creative Destruction
selected_sections: stylized facts; model; quantitative mechanism; predictions; robustness
teaching_function: Connects two facts to a general-equilibrium mechanism, closed-form intuition, quantitative implications, predictions, and alternative explanations.
transfer_limit: The long hybrid chain is useful when each layer is necessary; it is not a required amount of machinery.

title: A Dynamic Theory of Lending Standards
selected_sections: abstract; primitives; equilibrium; dynamics; externality; policy
teaching_function: Separates primitives, choices, equilibrium, steady state, dynamics, externalities, social optimum, and policy in a traceable theoretical progression.
transfer_limit: The proof density and fine section hierarchy should not be imitated as a formatting target.

title: Π-CAPM: The Classical CAPM with Probability Weighting and Skewed Assets
selected_sections: abstract; model nesting; prediction-to-test map
teaching_function: Shows how one model modification generates three discriminating predictions and maps each to stock, option, and correlation evidence.
transfer_limit: The preference specification is specialized and the predictions are not a general behavioral-finance template.
metadata_note: Official OUP title verified; the local MinerU/index title misread Π as 5.

title: The Cross Section of MBS Returns
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; data; theoretical predictions; empirical mapping; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses a simple pricing model to derive signed cross-sectional exposures, constructs the corresponding prepayment shocks, and then makes the theory-to-test mapping visible before estimating risk prices.
transfer_limit: The segmented MBS market and specialized-investor interpretation are unusual; predicted exposure signs do not by themselves prove who prices the risk.

title: Half Banked: The Economic Impact of Cash Management in the Marijuana Industry
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; institutional background; model; design; mechanism; conclusion
teaching_function: Turns an ordinarily ubiquitous service into an identifiable economic object, explains the unusual setting, and links price, quantity, cost, and profit margins through a model-guided empirical chain.
transfer_limit: The marijuana-industry regulations, IV, and traceability data are setting-specific; the 40% profitability estimate should not be generalized to ordinary banking access.

title: Nonstandard Errors
selected_sections: abstract; concept definition; project design; multiverse analysis; conclusion
teaching_function: Names a new source of empirical uncertainty, defines it by contrast with sampling error, and then gives repeated independent analyses, peer feedback, and a multiverse distinct evidentiary roles.
transfer_limit: The 164-team design and unusually large author/front-matter block are not manuscript templates; use the concept-to-design architecture only.

title: CEO Stress, Aging, and Death
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; measurement; complementary designs; robustness; limitations; conclusion
teaching_function: Combines a novel machine-learning outcome with a longer-run mortality outcome and two sources of variation, while acknowledging that the latent stress mechanism is not directly measured.
transfer_limit: Facial apparent age is a generated measure, and the two designs do not estimate an identical treatment; health interpretation must retain the paper's stated measurement limits.

title: Words Speak Louder without Actions
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; mechanism intuition; applications; conclusion
teaching_function: States a counterintuitive result in plain language, explains the two mechanism channels before formal detail, and returns to applications without pretending they are empirical tests.
transfer_limit: The principal-agent cheap-talk environment is specialized, and the memorable title or quotation should not become a generic theory-paper device.

title: Shrinking the Cross-Section
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; economic prior; methodology; out-of-sample evaluation; conclusion
teaching_function: Motivates high-dimensional shrinkage from an economic restriction, contrasts characteristic and principal-component sparsity, and makes out-of-sample performance the adjudicating evidence.
transfer_limit: The accepted-manuscript layout is not a current production template, and ridge-style shrinkage is not automatically appropriate for every predictor universe.
metadata_note: MinerU retains an Accepted Manuscript front page; title, DOI, and year use the strict final-publication inventory.

title: Empirical analysis of corporate tax reforms: What is the null and where did it come from?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; simulated experiments; power; empirical implications; conclusion
teaching_function: Shows how a theoretical model can interrogate the null, power, and welfare interpretation of a popular quasi-experimental design instead of treating a null estimate as decisive model rejection.
transfer_limit: The dynamic tax model is a diagnostic for a specific class of reforms; simulations do not invalidate difference-in-differences generally.

title: Quantifying the impact of red tape on investment: A survey data approach
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; survey measurement; identification; model mapping; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes respondent reporting behavior part of the measurement model, validates survey responses externally, and separates micro identification from aggregate model-implied costs.
transfer_limit: GDP losses remain conditional on the reporting model, normality, and equilibrium structure; survey complaints are not direct observations of causal wedges.

title: Measurement and effects of bank exit policies
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; construct measurement; credit-supply design; real effects; external validity; conclusion
teaching_function: Builds and validates a policy-strength measure before using it, then sequences lender compliance, firm financing, substitution, operations, and aggregate emissions as distinct claims.
transfer_limit: Coal is intentionally a high-exposure setting, the shift-share instrument has maintained assumptions, and estimated emissions changes are not a complete welfare calculation.

title: Credit and Social Unrest: Evidence from 1930s China
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; historical background; design; alternatives; external validity; conclusion
teaching_function: Compresses a historical shock and hand-collected outcomes into a clear causal chain and devotes the conclusion to magnitude-based external-validity conditions rather than a generic caveat.
transfer_limit: The silver-standard shock and political outcomes are historically specific; modern relevance depends on credit-shock magnitude and labor mobility.
metadata_note: MinerU retains a Journal Pre-proof front page.

title: Investor Memory
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; multi-experiment design; beliefs; behavior; mechanism; robustness; conclusion
teaching_function: Uses three experiments cumulatively: first establish selective recall, then connect recalled outcomes to beliefs and choices, and finally test a motivational account.
transfer_limit: The many subheadings reflect a multi-experiment design, not a general formatting target; laboratory memory mechanisms require care when extrapolating to field investors.

title: War Discourse and Disaster Premium: 160 Years of Evidence from the Stock Market
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; method; data; out-of-sample tests; mechanisms; conclusion
teaching_function: Solves a rare-event sample problem with long-run text data, makes rolling estimation and semantic change central to look-ahead control, and separates prediction from rational and behavioral interpretations.
transfer_limit: News discourse is an attention/perception proxy rather than objective disaster probability; a long historical sample does not eliminate model and semantic drift.

title: Is Capital Structure Irrelevant with ESG Investors?
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; benchmark theorem; deviations; empirical tests; conclusion
teaching_function: Extends a familiar irrelevance benchmark with explicit conditions, then uses empirical deviations to diagnose inconsistent attribution or segmentation rather than discarding the benchmark.
transfer_limit: The empirical evidence is described as suggestive, and a green-bond discount does not uniquely identify which benchmark condition fails.

title: A Theory of Liquidity Spillover between Bond and CDS Markets
selected_sections: abstract; introduction; model; key ingredients; robustness; testable predictions; conclusion
teaching_function: Makes one changed assumption—endogenous participation—responsible for reversing the standard result, identifies the key ingredients, and derives observable bond/CDS implications.
transfer_limit: The nondirected-search and participation environment is specific; policy statements about naked CDS bans remain model-dependent.
